P01.note: 'Its wheel turned in the open current, and the whole stream ran past it' strikes walled and siphoned on a surface read (nothing dams or draws off water), so only stilled competes with soured; stilled is the near-miss via 'held no trout or insect larvae' but the open current kills it.

P02.note: 'sealed crates, which were stacked unopened behind steel doors, with guards who let no one in' describes a depository outright; dump fails on a surface read because the museum chose the mine and took every crate back, and gallery/hospital are each killed by one planted phrase ('unopened', 'exactly as it had been packed').

P03.note: Each distractor has its own kill sentence ('library was a dozen books, all bought in the city' for scriptorium, 'kept no money overnight' for vault, 'In plague years it closed its gate' for sanatorium), so elimination is one-to-one; 'more of its income came from wine and beer sold to drovers' plus 'beds let by the night' then names a tavern almost directly.

P04.note: Relocation to an English village with shillings and English names points to naturalized; 'kept every chapter' kills mutilated, 'every drowning and every winter of hunger is told in full' kills lightened, and the after-blank rhythm sentence kills manicured - one planted kill per distractor.

P05.note: Bark chips, leaves and straw left on the soil, moisture through drought and suppressed weeds is a textbook mulch; manured is the near-miss (organic matter deposited) and, with leached, is killed by the after-blank 'same nitrogen' sentence, while mired is killed by 'drained off the field's sandy loam' and on-schedule planting.

P06.note: Cemetery fails on a surface read against 'voles that visit the strip outlive' the others; corridor is the real near-miss because the strip literally runs between the two forests, and 'none has been caught more than a few hundred yards from the forest it came from' kills it, with 'grass stems clipped of their seed heads' pointing to feeding.

P07.note: Visitors arriving from beyond the district for three hours, new restaurants and doubled rents give magnet; 'residents a tenth of the crowd' kills mixer and junction (the divided neighbourhoods are not brought together), and 'lawns ... slope open to the highway' kills muffler.

P08.note: Each of the photographs' sentences kills one distractor in turn: 'same mix of sizes at the cliffs as at the sea' (sorted), 'lying wherever they stopped' (stacked), 'same shade inside as out' (stained), leaving 'rounded to the hand' and 'gray with fine grit' for sanded; strong distractors but a strictly one-kill-per-sentence layout.

P09.note: Raised fails on a surface read against 'pressed it down a little more every summer' (and the stakes sentence); 'keeping to the same wheel tracks' gives rutted, and 'never cracked or shifted' at the braking stop sign kills both ruptured and rippled (shoving/washboarding).

P10.note: Needs the inference that water drawn 'from near the reservoir's floor' is cold, confirmed only by bass leaving and trout spawning; clogged is killed by the snowmelt still rolling the gravel bars, bled by bars 'as deep under water as before 1960', churned by 'at an even rate, day and night'.

P11.note: Level tracks 'like the treads of a stair' give furrowed (terraced would be more precise, which slightly weakens the key); 'grass grows as rough and tall' kills groomed and denuded, 'soil tests no richer' kills fertilized, but 'worn to bare earth' makes denuded a literal fit for the tracks themselves.

P12.note: Cold, oxygen-poor water with no boring worms, red paint, coiled ropes, wine in casks and oak hard enough to take a nail all say preserved; 'upright ... where it settled' kills jostled, 'on the open bottom' kills interred, and the intact cargo kills mined. Same world as P14 with the outcome inverted.

P13.note: Dislodged is a strong near-miss (stems weaving 'through and around the loose stones'), killed only by the after-blank gale sentence where the ivy half stood; 'Moisture readings ... matched' kills dried and 'stone faces under the stems were clean' kills etched.

P14.note: 'warm water where shipworms thrive' plus a plank 'light as cork' that crumbled gives gnawed; 'open sand that the current sweeps clean' kills entombed, 'outline unbroken' kills dismantled, 'smooth and pale on its surface' kills encrusted. Mirror of P12's world (merchant ship, iron bars and wine) with the opposite outcome, so solving one primes the other.

P15.note: Trellis fails on a surface read - nothing grows on the hull, which is 'furred with silt'; tomb is the stock wreck metaphor and is killed by 'crew were taken off by a passing schooner', tripwire by 'far below the keels of passing ships', and 'sixty chests of silver' in 'sealed holds' gives strongbox.

P16.note: Males circling females by the thousand reads as ballroom, but females losing a fifth of their weight shows spawning actually happened there, which supports bedroom (mating place) just as well, and 'For a few nights' adds to it; canteen is killed by the weight loss, clinic only weakly (the 'swarms of small fish' could be cleaners). Not exclusive between B and D.

P17.note: 'a scrolled frame laid with gold leaf' hands over gilded literally, so the figurative sense is never needed; 'The print is the survey's size' kills enlarged, 'north is at the top of both' kills flipped, 'every cape, bay, and shoal sits where the survey puts it' kills doctored, one sentence each.

P18.note: Wolves 'bedded in the willow thickets beside the crossings' with kills 'within three strides' gives ambushed and kills chased; 'The herd went on using the same crossings' and browsed willows kill cowed and corralled. Same world as P36 (wolves return, elk herd) with a different key.

P19.note: Needles browning each August and regrowing gives a surface-only scorched; 'growth rings were as wide' and beetles finding 'few hosts' kill sapped, 'large and small alike' kills winnowed, 'stayed standing for years' kills toppled - each by one planted clause.

P20.note: 'a third shorter: the weekly egg tallies and the daily notes on the wind are gone' gives tightened; 'nothing in the book comes from outside them' kills spliced, 'curses ... printed whole' kills softened, and 'misspellings ... included' kills tidied.

P21.note: 'ponds that cover the old meadow four feet deep, drowning the pines' states flooded literally; greened (the stock beaver word) is killed by the after-blank 'both valleys turn the same brown', deforested by willows that sprout again and aspens as thick, dredged by silt raising the pond floors.

P22.note: The 1791 fire burning every cottage while the orchard lost only scorched leaves gives firebreak; frost blackening 'those beside the wall too' kills hearth, 'the river lies a mile to the south' kills dike, 'open at both ends' kills fence - one kill sentence per distractor.

P23.note: The banding experiment rules out the expected ant-plant roles ('flowered, podded and grew as well' kills pollinated and parasitized, 'caterpillars chewed both alike' kills patrolled), and the after-blank seed sentence (oily knob, young shrubs on ant mounds fifty yards away) must be combined to reach propagated.

P24.note: Hundreds crowding in and stripping the flesh in four months gives banquet; cupboard and battery are near-misses for a stored food source and fail only on the speed ('in four months', 'scattered as soon as the flesh was gone'), and 'animals found across the whole seafloor' kills bridge.

P25.note: Mud in, clear water out and a rising floor show the marsh traps sediment, while 'carried all the creek's fertilizer nitrate on into the bay' kills kidney (filters but passes the solute) and the oxygen sentence kills lung; kitchen is not cleanly killed - 'Nearby shrimp were full of plankton' reads as support for it as easily as against.

P26.note: Costumed villagers acting out the village's history at six stops for paying spectators gives pageant; roundup is killed by carriages 'scattering the grazing ponies', pilgrimage has no religious content though the dawn walk to the far edge fits it loosely, and raid literally names the 1460 attack the last scene depicts.

P27.note: Her weakest stanza printed 'beside a cartoon of a weeping cow' is mockery, so panned; 'who held the only plates' kills pirated, 'printing her name over' the stanza kills plagiarized, 'sold forty copies' kills popularized.

P28.note: Tripled price, halved circulation, closures and lay-offs give impoverished; muzzled (the stock wartime-press word) is killed by 'printed whatever they pleased' and the after-blank attacks on the tax and war, nationalized by 'stayed in private hands', mobilized by the same attacks.

P29.note: Roadmap fails on a surface read - nothing in the passage concerns routes or places; recipe is killed by 'Each line pairs a man's name with the barley he was given', and receipt is the near-miss, ruled out by twelve monthly tablets with the same nine names kept in the temple storeroom under the overseer's seal.

P30.note: Aphids kept in place and scattering where ants could not reach gives herded, but 'Aphids on leaves a worker had crossed crept a third as fast' and fewer growing wings literally describes a sedative trace, so drugged is defensible as the mechanism; garnered is killed (the ants take honeydew, not aphids), and devoured is weakened by clusters growing all summer but the unreached row holding three times as many gives it some support.

P31.note: Foreign basalt boulders strewn across the meadows give littered, and 'frozen fast to the ground' with the soil surviving kills incised and milled; but the glacier 'filled a mountain valley' and 'lay there for several thousand years', so mantled literally describes what the passage reports and is not killed.

P32.note: 'a lookout on the bow of one could not make out its own stern' hands over blinded by itself; 'a steady breeze kept every ship moving' kills becalmed and 'reaching harbor afloat and unharmed' kills beached and capsized together.

P33.note: 'he dosed miners from the bottles with quinine and laudanum by weights copied from a physician's handbook ... charges each man by the dose' describes a pharmacy outright; repository is a literal fit for the safe holding laudanum and takings, parlor rests only on the shelf of bottles and stove, and pawnshop is not supported by credit against a cleanup.

P34.note: 'broke open the cases and filled their packs ... leaving slashed canvases on the floor' hands over ransacked; 'Nothing was listed' kills requisitioned, 'asked for nothing' kills ransomed, and pieces surfacing 'in shops across the army's home country' kills repatriated, whose bait (the city's fleet looted neighbouring towns) is planted only to be refuted.

P35.note: Winter snow released as summer flow exactly when the plain's streams dry and the ditches open must be combined to reach storeroom; 'level hardly changes between morning and night' kills timepiece, 'held one rock ledge ... through warm decades and cold' kills thermometer, 'seen only from the last village' kills signpost.

P36.note: Rejuvenated fails on a surface read against 'the herd grew older'; 'held as many elk in winter as ever' and 'its total barely changed' kill reduced, 'kept to their old ranges' kills redistributed, and constant head-raising and bolting 'at a raven's call' give rattled. Same world as P18.

P37.note: Ships waiting for a licensed pilot and a council-set fee that 'paved the town's streets' give tollbooth; 'three or four at a time' kills turnstile, 'tied up at the town's piers to unload' kills wharf, and swells rolling over the bar to break against the piers kills seawall.

P38.note: A cratered depot and rubble give bombarded; 'Alliance warships stood off the harbor' makes blockaded a literal fit, killed by 'freighters of every flag still came and went', while the wool still selling in the alliance's markets kills boycotted and the island's flag still flying kills annexed.

P39.note: Taken down stone by stone, numbered and raised again across the ocean gives crated, though 'the council crated the church' is an awkward collocation (the council sold it; workers packed it); 'walls sound and its tower true' kills condemned, 'stone by stone' kills bulldozed, 'had paid the town for it' kills commandeered.

P40.note: New floors laid over yearly sand, a well through thirty feet of sand to the first street and a ramp up to the gate must be combined to reach lifted; 'all inside the same circuit of walls' kills nibbled, the ramp and caravans still arriving kill imprisoned, and 'Wind slowing in the still air behind its walls' kills lashed.

tells: Paired near-duplicate worlds with different keys: P12/P14 (merchant ship carrying iron bars and wine sunk off a coast, divers in 1990 - mummified vs gnawed) and P18/P36 (wolves return to a mountain valley, one elk herd - ambushed vs rattled). Solving one primes the other, and the repeated frame shows the template.

One planted kill per distractor: on most items each wrong option is contradicted by its own sentence or clause, usually phrased as 'the same as / as before / still / never / none' (P03, P04, P05, P08, P09, P10, P11, P13, P14, P17, P19, P20, P21, P22, P27, P28, P34, P35, P36, P37, P38, P40). A solver can find the three negated words and pick the leftover without reading the passage as an argument; explicit_kills is 3 on most of the render.

A sentence AFTER the blank that kills the strongest near-miss: P04 (rhythm kills manicured), P05 ('same nitrogen' kills manured/leached), P07 (rents), P13 (gale kills dislodged), P21 ('same brown' kills greened), P28 (attacks kill muzzled), P30 (unreached row), P31 (river between boulders). Recognisable shape: claim with blank, then one closing sentence aimed at the stock word.

The stock collocation for the scenario is consistently the distractor, killed by one planted fact: corridor (P06), tomb (P15), greened (P21), muzzled (P28), dislodged (P13), blockaded (P38), sorted (P08), manured (P05). A test-wise solver who learns that the obvious word is always wrong gains an edge.

Alliterative or same-initial option sets used repeatedly: P06 (cage/corridor/cemetery/cafeteria), P08 (stacked/sanded/sorted/stained), P09 (raised/rutted/ruptured/rippled), P10 (chilled/clogged/churned + bled), P23 (patrolled/propagated/pollinated/parasitized), P27 (pirated/plagiarized/panned/popularized), P29 (receipt/recipe/roadmap), P34 (ransacked/ransomed/repatriated/requisitioned), P36 (redistributed/reduced/rejuvenated/rattled). Not key-predictive by itself but an obvious shared template.

Metaphor-noun frame 'X served as / called the Y's ______' recurs across P02, P03, P06, P07, P15, P16, P22, P24, P25, P26, P29, P33, P35, P37; the key is always the noun naming the function the evidence describes.
